Wouldn't it be great if you could hear, see the songs on other people's computers completely over a wireless network and stream them and listen to their music if they give you permission.

I can find out what music my kids are listening to if they let me.

You just connect it with your computer and your entire music library is synced onto your iPod.

You want to listen to music around your house.
So what do you do?
It turns out that there is a huge iPod economy out there.

And you just pop your iPod in it, you've got a stereo to go.
Runs on batteries or runs with an adapter in the wall.
This has been huge.

These things are not in the same room and you don't really want to run wires.

It's amazing.
And this is in just a little over one year.
Uh, the iTunes music store has a 70% market share of all legal downloads.
70%.
But, that's only been interesting if you've lived in the US until today.
Because today we're introducing the iTunes music store into the UK, Germany, and France.
Now, these three countries represent over 60% of current European music sales.
62%.

UK, Germany, and France.
Now, before we show you the store, uh, or the stores, uh, I want to go back to the beginning and talk about the philosophy behind iTunes.
Uh, and there's no better place to start than who does iTunes really compete with?
Now, in the US you might say it's Napster, Rhapsody, and Music Match.
Uh, over here in Europe you might say it's OD2 and Virgin.
But this isn't really true because iTunes has a 70% market share.
All the rest of these guys put together, you know, are 30%.
It's not really who iTunes competes with.
Who iTunes really competes with is this.
It's piracy.
This is the big market for downloads.
And if you don't think it's so big, take a look at this.
This is what the piracy, this is how piracy has impacted the music market in these countries.
It's brought it to its knees in the UK with zero growth last year.
But that's phenomenal compared to what it's done in Germany and France.
The market shrunk in Germany by 19% and it shrunk in France by 14%.
So piracy is a really big market and this is our competitor.
So if you're going to compete with piracy, you have to understand it and you have to offer a better product.

When you go, how many of you've downloaded a song illegally?

I tried it.
Yeah, because I market research.

So the song downloads really slow.

And you have to try several times before you actually get the song.
But when you finally get the song, you find that it was encoded by a 10-year-old and the last four seconds is cut off.

How are we going to offer a better product?

Next, we're going to replace unreliable encoding with perfect encoding.
We encode everything ourselves, we check everything.
Uh, it's it's great.

Obviously, we're going to give you great album cover art and it's not stealing.
It's good karma.

I want to buy it, I want to own it for all time.
I don't want anyone to tell me I can't listen to it 10 years from now if I stop stop paying a subscription fee.
So in iTunes, you own the music, there are no subscription fees.
Unlimited CD burning.

We put a limit on how many times you can burn a single playlist, which is seven, which is anywhere from two to four more than anyone else gives you.
But each track you can burn an unlimited number of times.
So you can always have your favorite song on every CD you burn.
You can play your music on up to five computers.
This is two more than we started with.
And you can mix and match, max and PCs.
You can have all PCs, all Macs, or any combination in between.
And an unlimited number of iPods.
CD burning is getting less important as people have iPods.

So, again, you own the music, no subscription fees.
Unlimited CD burning for personal use.
Burn any playlist up to seven times.
An unlimited number of iPods and you can play it on up to five computers, PC and Mac.
And this this last point's key.
You can authorize and deauthorize your computers.
So if you've got your music on five computers and you want to get rid of one, donate it to your school and buy a new one, let's say, you can deauthorize that one you're going to donate and free up a slot and authorize the new computer.
So as you grow and migrate from computer to computer, your music can follow you.
So these are landmark personal use rights.

They really are the gold standard of personal use rights in the uh, legal online business.

Very, very easy.

This is really important.

No can do.

Run it on your PCs all you want.
